plugin.name: Build Apple Apps
plugin.description: Bring the iOS Simulator into the activity panel: the agent builds, installs and launches your app while you watch and use it live, with a built-in SwiftUI guide covering both patterns and diagnosis.
tab.label: Simulator
panel.starting: Starting the simulator preview… The first run downloads serve-sim and may boot a simulator, which can take a minute.
panel.idle: The simulator preview is not running.
panel.unsupported.title: macOS only
panel.unsupported.body: The iOS Simulator relies on Xcode and CoreSimulator, so it runs on macOS only.
panel.failed: The simulator preview failed to start
panel.failedHint: It needs an Apple Silicon Mac with Xcode and at least one iOS simulator runtime installed. The output below shows what went wrong.
panel.commandDisabled.title: Allow the plugin to run npx
panel.commandDisabled.body: The preview is started with npx, which Vetta does not allow until you switch it on. Open Abilities, select Build Apple Apps, turn on npx under Executable commands, then choose Retry.
panel.openExternalFailed: Could not open the preview in the browser
settings.title: Build Apple Apps
settings.subtitle: Preview service and panel options
settings.tagline: Watch and use an iOS Simulator right in the activity panel, on the same device the agent builds and runs your app on.
settings.service.heading: Simulator preview
settings.service.running: Running on port {{port}} (bound to this Mac only).
settings.service.unsupported: The iOS Simulator is supported on macOS only.
settings.service.hint: The plugin runs {{package}} through Vetta's built-in Node runtime on a host-allocated local port, and stops it when the plugin is disabled or the app quits.
settings.options.heading: Panel options
settings.options.alwaysShowTab.title: Always show the simulator tab
settings.options.alwaysShowTab.descripti: By default the tab appears only in directories recognised as an Xcode or SwiftPM project. Turn this on when the project is not at the repository root.
settings.options.autoStartServer.title: Start the preview when the panel opens
settings.options.autoStartServer.descrip: When off, start it manually from the panel — useful if you would rather not keep a background process running.
settings.footer.credit: The simulator preview is provided by serve-sim (Apache-2.0), the same mirror OpenAI's Codex uses. Apple Silicon only. With Xcode 27, keyboard input needs the simulator window visible in Device Hub and Vetta allowed under Privacy & Security → Accessibility.
settings.footer.agent: On the agent side a built-in Skill drives the simulator with xcrun simctl and xcodebuild only, and pulls in the SwiftUI component, Liquid Glass and performance-audit guides on demand.
keyboard.title: Typing doesn't reach the simulator.
keyboard.accessibility: With Xcode 27, keys are forwarded through Device Hub, which needs Vetta allowed under System Settings → Privacy & Security → Accessibility. Allow it, then restart the preview from the plugin settings. Taps and swipes still work.
keyboard.device-hub: With Xcode 27, keys are forwarded through Device Hub. Open Device Hub and show the {{device}} window (it can stay in the background). Taps and swipes still work.
keyboard.window: With Xcode 27, keys are forwarded through the {{device}} window in Device Hub. Open that window and keep it Device Hub's current window (it can stay in the background). If it is already open, this is a known serve-sim issue with Xcode 27 on macOS 27 (it cannot find Device Hub's process); typing will work once a fixed serve-sim is released and this plugin updates to it. Taps and swipes still work.
keyboard.other: Keys could not be forwarded through Device Hub. Taps and swipes still work.
